message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What Happens | |---------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points are earned by being the first to finish each round. | | **Setup** | • 108‑card deck (standard Uno deck).
• Each player draws 7 cards.
• Place the remaining cards face down to form the draw pile.
• Turn the top card of the draw pile face up to start the discard pile. | | **Turn Order** | Players take turns clockwise (unless a direction‑changing card is played). | | **Playing a Card** | On your turn you may play one card from your hand that matches the discard pile’s **color**, **number**, or **symbol**. If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile. | | **Special Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Drawing** | If you draw a playable card, you may play it immediately. If not, your turn ends. | | **Going Out** | When you play your last card, shout “Uno!” (if you’re down to one card). If you forget, the next player can call you out and you must draw two cards as a penalty. | | **Scoring** | After a player goes out, all other players add the point values of the cards left in their hands:
• Number cards = face value
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points
• The winner of the round gets the sum of all other players’ points. | | **Winning** | First player to reach the agreed‑upon total (e.g., 500) wins the game. | **Optional House Rules** - *Stacking*: Allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing. - *No “Wild Draw Four” unless you have no matching color* (official rule). - *“Uno” penalty*: Some groups require a penalty if you forget to say “Uno.” That’s the core of Uno—simple, fast, and a lot of fun!
